correctness.rationale: For each received row w of length n−1, distinct one-insertion supersequences I_q(w) partition disjointly by whether the initial received symbol is retained, proving |I_q(w)|=1+n(q−1). The product I_q(u)×I_q(v) is restricted by coordinatewise x_j≤y_j. Induction on n partitions by the two first symbols a,b. For a≤b, the count is ≤M_(n−1)+(q−1+b−a)T+q(q−1)/2−(b−a), with T=1+(n−1)(q−1), maximized at b−a=q−1, yielding M_n. For a>b, count ≤qT+q(q−1)/2<M_n for n≥2. At u=0^(n−1), v=(q−1)^(n−1), there are (1+n(q−1))² possible row supersequence pairs, with exactly nq(q−1)/2 incompatible same-position exceptional pairs. Equality in the bound forces every leading pair (a,b)=(0,q−1), proving unique receiver for n>=2; n=1 returns q(q+1)/2. Independent direct exhaustive enumeration on seven (q,n) parameter pairs corroborated all base/equality cases.

Dollma et al. Section V and Appendix D give average deletion ball sizes for radius (1,0) and radius 1, not the simultaneous (1,1) exact worst inverse list.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Sphere packing and error correction yield neither the quadratic expression for all inverse list sizes nor the unique extremizing read pair without this compatibility subtraction and equality-case induction.

evidence: The submitted exact receiver inverse list counts distinct componentwise ordered source pairs after exactly one deletion in each of two labeled rows.
Dollma et al. mostly treat channel deletion in one of two rows and code cardinality; Ye et al. define more general deletion-error models but bound and construct codebooks.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: One deletion in either row, deletion ball size, or code redundancy is not the same as the inverse size of a fixed pair of two deleted reads. No equivalent sharp expression occurs in inspected main theorems.
